If it’s possible to have multi-account ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-24209|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-24209|smart-link]), then we could allocate some accounts in advance, like 4-8. During role generation, we could use a hashcode of a service name to assign it to the account. It's something like a consistent hash. This would be the most straightforward approach.

It would be much more difficult to implement if we had to maintain a mapping between the service and the IAM account. The builder would have to deploy services only to pre-defined clusters (assigned IAM account). Configless script would have to retrieve config from the builder to create a role for a correct IAM account. We will need to design IAM accounts in a way to be able to provide resources (not only secrets, any AWS resource like S3, sns/sqs etc) for different IAM accounts. For me, it looks like about ~2 months of work in a collaboration with the SRE team.

{color:#006644}+*BANK GUARANTEE DOCUMENT*+ {color}

This document is an add-on to the original agreement (MoU) between Bolt and the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. It introduces two new things:

# *Bank Guarantee*

* Bolt agrees to provide a bank guarantee  (a financial safety net) for a set amount.
* This guarantee will be held by the Borough to make sure Bolt sticks to the obligations set out in the MoU.
* If Bolt doesn’t meet its obligations (like not paying fees or causing damage), the Borough can use this guarantee to cover costs. 

# *Per Bike Fee*

* Bolt agrees to pay a maximum of £20 per bike that it operates in the Borough.
* The Borough agrees it won’t charge more than this per bike - no hidden or extra fees.

# *General provisions*

* This Addendum starts on the date it’s signed and stays in place as long as the original MoU is active.
* If the original MoU ends, the Borough will return the bank guarantee (unless they need to deduct any costs due to Bolts non-compliance).
* The rules in this Addendum are governed by the laws of England and Wales.
* The rest of the original MoU remains unchanged and valid.

[~accountid:712020:1d5390cd-af56-43c8-9d12-f431b20183ba] As a first step I recommend you push back on signing this bank guarantee. The reason is a bank guarantee will usually mean that Bolt will need to set aside cash or credit to back the guarantee. Additionally, the Borough can call on the bank guarantee if they believe there's been non-compliance - even before a dispute is fully resolved. This could result in the Borough taking funds without Bolt agreeing that the breach occurred. The current drafting of the Addendum is quite broad ("including but not limited to failure to meet operational requirements, payment obligations, or damages"). This gives the Borough wide discretion to call on the guarantee, even for relatively minor or disputed issues.

[~accountid:712020:1d5390cd-af56-43c8-9d12-f431b20183ba] However, if the guarantee is unavoidable then you should liaise with the Borough to negotiate for a lower or capped amount based on the expected value at risk, rather than a blanket figure (currently this field is blank in the Addendum). You should also ask the Borough to narrow the wording of the guarantee so that it can only be drawn on in very specific, material circumstances (e.g., repeated failure to comply after written notice and opportunity to rectify) as well as asking for a cure period which is a chance for Bolt to fix the issue (e.g., *_within 14 or 30 days_*) before drawing on the guarantee.

[~accountid:712020:1d5390cd-af56-43c8-9d12-f431b20183ba] If the guarantee is unavoidable, please speak with the accounting team (Cc: [~accountid:5c8677321f6ea3234ddaa682] ) and any other relevant teams at Bolt, as Legal can’t authorise providing a bank guarantee. Do reach out to them to discuss the practicalities and next steps.

Please feel free to reach out to me on Slack if you have any questions.

The pilot will consist of the deployment of 3 AI Agents (think of these as field counsels).

*Deployment and Integration:* 2 -3 weeks - integration into existing tools slack, emails and JIRA (including signature tools) - as if a field counsel would be answering the queries. There is no additional UX or platform to access.

*New Zealand (NZ)*

Bolt can rely on its standard approach of *soft opt-in marketing* in New Zealand for its Rides vertical based on advice from external counsel.

Specifically, Bolt relies on *inferred consent* under the *Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 (UEMA)* to send commercial electronic messages to existing customers. This is permissible where there is an *existing business relationship* and the message is relevant to the recipient’s prior engagement with Bolt.
{panel}

# Ensure it has inferred consent for each message:green-check: 
## Inferred Consent used for Bolt’s “consent_promotions_and_tips” and “Bolt’s offers”;
## Partner Offers are still opt-in (express) consent based same as standard approach dictates.
# Clearly identify itself as the sender:green-check: 
# Include a functional unsubscribe facility that is effective within 5 working days and valid for at least 30 days after the message is sent
## Bolt’s unsubscribe takes affect within 72 hours and is permanent;:green-check: 
## Bolt is also currently revising its global approach to unsubscribe to ensure that 1 unsubscribe request unsubscribes from all direct marketing, and not just a category to which the received message was sent.:loading:

Hi. Tax code itself doesn’t impact RC accounting at all. It depends only on _tax applicability_. 

* In this case there is *_VAT EU Acquisitions of Services - Reverse Charge Non Recoverable_* - so automatically _Tax Recoverability_ is populated as *_Nonrecoverable + Allocate_* (we have default tax recoverability for each tax applicability item, though it can be changed manually on the invoice if needed - not recommended).
* _Tax Recoverability_ identifies accounting for VAT amounts.
** If Tax recoverability = +Recoverable+ then Accounting is Debit _2305:Reverse purchases VAT_ Credit _2304:Reverse sales VAT_ 
** If Tax recoverability = +Non Recoverable+ then Accounting is Debit _Spend account_ {color:#97a0af}_(VAT allocated along with net amount)_ {color}Credit _2304:Reverse sales VAT_

Inputs from Lisanna in regards to tool reporting.



* *Tracking number of requests per country, per authority, per vertical?*
** Reporting on requests per country and per vertical is available. Requests per authority is not tracked, we can only differentiate "law enforcement" vs "government authority"
* *How many have a legal basis and how many do not?*
** This data is not collected. If a request does not have a legal basis, we ask for it. If still not provided, we decline the disclosure of data.
* *Did it come from an official authority?*
** This data is not collected. If a request doesn't come from an official domain, we decline the disclosure of data.
* *Do we have a specific person who sends the request*
** Not sure why this is relevant? Requests can come from any investigating police officers. It's never a specific requestor.
* *List of legal basis*
** This info is included in the [Authority Requests - Market Specific Info|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/19F9dMxdObEnLmTW4PazyKso7fM5c7SSkUwPsON2X1Ow/edit?gid=0#gid=0] sheet
* *Is the request proportional or justified?*
** This data is not collected. If the request is not justified or proportional, we decline the disclosure of data.
* *Frequency of reports?*
** Per person
** Rider detail
** Driver detail
*** None of this data is collected. We do however add a comment on the Rider/Driver profile if an LER involving them is received.
* *Link to the doc(with limited access)*
** This data is not collected
* *Reporter name*
** This data is not collected

Xtrabackup 2.4 backup files are not compatible with Xtrabackup 8.0, which makes direct restoration impossible between versions. 

While it is technically feasible to install Xtrabackup 2.4 on Ubuntu 20.04 and 22.04, this approach is complicated by the existing presence of Xtrabackup 8.0 and the unavailability of the Perforna Office Debian repository, making package management and version switching cumbersome.

A more straightforward and reliable solution is to use a Docker container running Xtrabackup 2.4. This method isolates dependencies and avoids interference with the current system setup.

Alternatively, the file copy method eliminates dependency concerns entirely. However, this approach requires downtime on the source MySQL 5.7 instance and may result in significant replication lag when dealing with large datasets.

Thanks for tagging me into the ticket. I have reviewed your query on whether Section 20 would serve as a valid legal basis for a Home Office caseworker requesting personal data of a Bolt driver and this IMO would depend on the specific circumstances of the request. In general, there are a few key points to consider:

The request for personal data under Section 20 must align with a purpose related to immigration control. If the caseworker is seeking information for reasons that are directly tied to assessing immigration status, eligibility, or compliance with immigration law, then this section could potentially serve as a valid legal basis.

The caseworker must be requesting information that is necessary for fulfilling their role related to immigration enforcement or assessment. If the personal data of the Bolt driver is necessary for such purposes (e.g., verifying residency status or work eligibility), this could be valid.

The request must also be proportionate and not excessive given the nature of the case. This means that the Home Office must ensure they are only requesting the minimum amount of personal data needed to fulfil the purpose.

+*To summarise*+

Section 20 of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 could be a valid legal basis for a Home Office caseworker to request personal data of a Bolt driver, provided the request is for a legitimate immigration-related purpose and is compliant with data protection requirements. It would be advisable for Bolt to review the exact nature of the request and ensure that any data shared is done so within the legal parameters.

If you need any further support or have additional questions, I’d suggest looping in [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a], who is a UK-qualified privacy lawyer and better placed to advise on this given his expertise.

Hi [~accountid:5d8df399c7d4e30dc2836580] , There is *no explicit* clause in the T&Cs that allows Bolt to automatically offboard or terminate a driver due to inactivity or non-use of the platform for a certain period

However, under Clause 13.3 of the Bolt Ireland Driver T&Cs, Bolt can terminate the agreement with 30 days' notice and provide a reason, and the reasons listed (like reputational risk, breach, changes to the platform, etc.) are non-exhaustive:

_“Bolt Ireland may terminate this Agreement... by giving you at least 30 days' notice together with Bolt Ireland’s reasons for doing so.”_

So, while a reason must technically be given, it doesn’t need to be serious or specific, The clause gives broad discretion to Bolt. In practice, Bolt could give a reason like _"to ensure the normal ongoing operation of the platform"_ (Clause 13.3.1) or _"due to prolonged inactivity impacting operational efficiency"_ (if needed), and that would likely suffice under the terms.

Please note that the same amount of time would be required for new T&Cs to become effective. 

Let me know if you have any questions. 

BR,

Iva

So I don’t see what could be changed right now, as agents should already consider the duplicate ticket as a confirmation. Following from last week, FinReg view is that enabling early cashouts in Canada (under the AWX solution) is compliant with FinReg rules, as long as Bolt does not charge from the driver a fee higher than the cost paid to AWX and the cost paid to AWX is more or less aligned with the market standard. This is because Bolt cannot be seen to generate revenue or commercial advantage from the activity of “providing or maintaining an account” for the drivers. Charging a limited amount of fee directly related to AWX cost ensures that our “providing or maintaining an account” is incidental to our main activity of offering a ride-hailing marketplace. 

*Comment for local Legal team* [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e]: 

Overall the rollout should follow the general [+Early cashouts legal approach+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-k577syght9UZMbQG-QoKbdqKEMefhhnTVWjlsGfQB0/edit?tab=t.0], including T&Cs wordings and need for any local validations regarding potential credit activity. General analysis on the risk of early cashouts activity potentially qualifying as credit activity is provided in the legal approach doc.

In marketing/advertising/communications where we draw attention to either the regular payouts or early payouts feature of our platform, we should add a note/disclaimer that payment services to drivers are provided by Airwallex and that no payment services are provided by Bolt. [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] I will also schedule a call for us so I can explain a bit more about the FinReg rules we need to apply in Canada, including for marketing communications.

h2. Hard block investigation

* Conceptually scheduled block is a *suspension*, and hard block (aka partner block aka root-level block) is a *termination*. You can find more info in this [Slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01PT0B6D70/p1743770402900879].
* We have some use-cases that prevent us from moving fully from hard blocks to scheduled blocks:
** For scheduled blocks there is no duplication checks during sign-up. Basically driver with scheduled block can create a new account and drive with Bolt again.
** Scheduled block is applied to Driver account. But the same Person can have several Driver accounts. Although we can develop functionality that will schedule block all the Driver accounts of the same Person, there is still a problem with new accounts.
** Visibility/UI problem. Schedule blocks look like a temporary suspension (even if infinite) to CS, so they might override Fraud’s decision to block the driver, if driver contacts support. With hard blocks Fraud has more control of the unblocking process.
* Fraud does ~60 hard blocks weekly. We might be overdoing them ([~accountid:5cefa65be2e3ec0fc196de31] is doing a research on whether we can be less harsh with the blocking).
* Legal wants us to go through blocking machine, so in the end we should fully integrate with the blocking machine
* There is an idea of partner-based blocks on the horizon. It’s not implemented/planned yet. More info [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/6178701398/Partner-based+scheduled+blocking+not+implemented+yet].



*Soft decision:* integrate hard blocks with manual review system (the same way they are integrated now with scheduled blocks). Can be done by us, but requires alignment with the team that owns manual review system.

* disable motor output until the throttle returns to 0-deadzone

** after decelerated to 0 km/h

*19E & 20E* (right *AND* left brake lever not in original position error):

* disable error from being animated on display
* don't disable motor output when there are error conditions

*18E, 19E, 20E* (throttle *AND* right *AND* left brake lever not in original position error):

* keep the errors only for IOT broadcasting, so we can check vehicles which still have problems through our backend.{quote}

Under the *Article 13.1* of the Terms and Conditions, the courier is solely responsible for the performance of the Delivery Agreement and for any claims made under the Delivery Agreement. Bolt is not liable for any failure to perform or incomplete performance of the Delivery Agreement and does not assume liability for any traffic violation or accident that occurs during the performance of the Delivery Agreement. 


The above clause means that Bolt shall in no case take responsibility for a courier’s failure to perform the Delivery Agreement, including any accidents that may occur during the performance of the Delivery Agreement, which, amongst other things, shall include damage caused to third-party property.


The *Article 13.4* of the Terms and Conditions states that the courier shall defend, indemnify and hold Bolt harmless from and against any and all claims, lawsuits, actions or administrative proceedings, demands, damages and expenses of any kind, including attorneys’ fees and costs, arising out of or in connection with the Delivery Partner’s provision of delivery services under the General Terms and Conditions.


The above-mentioned clause is of a very broad nature indicating that the courier is responsible for protecting Bolt from any legal or financial consequences that arise from the courier’s actions while providing delivery services. So, based on this clause, if the courier’s actions cause harm or damage to a third party while performing delivery services, Bolt can ask the courier to pay for the damages and cover all related expenses, including legal costs. This is essentially a protective measure for Bolt, ensuring that Bolt is not financially liable for the actions of the courrier during the delivery service.

Hope this helps, but please let me know if you have any further questions. Thank you.

INSERT_RATE = 100  # per second

def get_row_count():
    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM queue_table")
    return cursor.fetchone()['count']

def insert_rows(n):
    query = "INSERT INTO queue_table (data) VALUES (%s)"
    values = [("Test row",) for _ in range(n)]
    cursor.executemany(query, values)
    conn.commit()

def delete_rows(n):
    cursor.execute("SELECT id FROM queue_table ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT %s", (n,))
    ids = cursor.fetchall()
    if ids:
        id_list = [str(row['id']) for row in ids]
        id_string = ",".join(id_list)
        cursor.execute(f"DELETE FROM queue_table WHERE id IN ({id_string})")
        conn.commit()

def main():
    try:
        while True:
            start_time = time.time()

            # Insert batch
            insert_rows(INSERT_RATE)

            # Trim the table if over max size
            current_count = get_row_count()
            if current_count > MAX_ROWS:
                delete_rows(current_count - MAX_ROWS)

            # Maintain 1 second pace
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            time.sleep(max(0, 1.0 - elapsed))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("Stopped by user.")
    finally:
        cursor.close()
        conn.close()

~ Summary below ~

h3. *Subject: Driver Data Access and AML/KYC Compliance for Fleet Partnerships in Taiwan*

h4. *1. Driver Data in Fleet Portal*

* The Privacy Team requested the full list of driver data accessible by fleet managers in Taiwan, for inclusion in Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs).
* Sudipto confirmed that Fleet Operators can access:
** *Driver Details*: contact data, username, full name, avatar, suspension history, and list of uploaded documents (not the documents themselves).
** *Performance Metrics*: activity time/location, order details, feedback, earnings, vehicle details, and aggregated performance indicators.
** *Dispatching Settings*: categories available, cash trips, and potentially: opt-out settings, B2B orders, destinations, and radius.

----

h4. *2. AML/KYC Data Collection Requirements*

* Privacy asked which individuals' data must be collected under AML/KYC regulations.
* Stanley Wu confirmed collection is required from:
** Company responsible person
** Directors
** Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) (≥25% ownership)
** Senior management or a representative, if UBOs can’t be identified
* Alon clarified that *consent is not needed* under Taiwan’s PDPA when data is collected to comply with legal obligations. Instead, individuals must be *notified* (e.g., via a disclaimer or privacy notice).

----

h4. *3. Regulatory Basis and Interpretation*

* The team reviewed and translated AML/CTF regulations and guidelines applicable to Third-Party Payment Service Providers (TPPSPs).
* Stanley pointed to relevant sections in Articles 7, 8, 11 and Q&A clarifications defining UBOs and senior management roles.
* We confirmed that data collection is *justified under law*, and the *Privacy Team approved* the collection of this data for AML purposes.
* The team emphasized that the *Information Form must include a disclaimer* explaining the legal basis for this data collection.

----

h4. *4. Privacy Notice vs. Information Form*

* It was clarified that the *Privacy Notice currently covers only drivers and passengers*, not third parties like fleet representatives.
* Therefore, the *Information Form must include a disclaimer* about data collected for AML/KYC, as this is currently the only way to fulfill PDPA notification requirements for these individuals.

* Overcharge decisions → price to zero cases
* Order rejections → cases where the order is reverted into reject state through fraud signaling
* Signals to quality → fraud alerts the quality team of problems on trip
* Signals from quality → quality also reviews the partner, applies their own restrictions and training; often also on the same topics (double actioning)

* In how many cases we see any other fraud but only action based the RDNH scenarios?
** Including scenarios of quality signaling

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Fleet owner was hacked ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet-company/companies/edit/105550?tab=profile]) - Paris Fleet JIR TRANSPORTS. Hacker changed and phone number.
* Hacker was able to subsequently change bank details due to CS error.
** On 24 March 2025, hacker messaged CS (Achim Sebti) in app ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/543262800]) asking to change RIB (bank identity statement). Hacker provided selfie with ID (CS seem to be suggesting that this was sourced from previous tickets - see [this|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/537755167] ticket from 14 March - and so is fake).
** CS responded asking for: (i) manually signed bank details from; and (ii) a company registration document (KBIS) dated on that day’s date.
** Hacker provided KBIS, but incorrect date. Hacker also provided bank details form, but not manually signed (clearly digitally edited).
** CS changed the bank details on 27 March 2025 as a result.
* Hacker successfully redirected a payout of EUR 2769.37.
* On 3 April, this was discovered by the genuine account owner and reported to CS ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/549284334]).
** FO mentioned EUR 2769.37 not paid into their account, and they have drivers to pay.
** FO confirmed that the previous conversation with CS was not them.
** Apparently, email and phone changed again on 3 April.
* On 4 April, CS disabled payments from the account. FO now concerned that they cannot pay their drivers as a result.
* According to Jo Grossi ([here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C019YPJMGSC/p1743606632608929]) the hacker still has access to the fleet portal.
** Unbelievably, it seems there have been a few discussions about the incident ([here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05B4K0H0R0/p1743754239682599]), but no-one has done anything to resolve it.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* This seems to be a clear data breach. Regardless of whether the fleet company is an individual or a company, the hacker used a selfie and ID card to secure the change of bank details, and so at least some personal data has been breached here.
** I have therefore reported this to the ODPO team here.
* It is not clear to me how the hacker gained access to the FO’s account. This needs to be confirmed with CS.
* It is not clear to me the full extent of data that has been breached here - in particular, we need to know if the hacker has access to the data on other drivers.
* It does not appear that we have taken steps to kick the scammer out, nor to change any of the details back. The longer we leave this, the higher the risk and the more likely it is tat we need to notify the breach. 

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Is the fleet owner an individual or a company?
* How did the hacker gain access to the account in the first place (to change phone number and email)? When did this happen?
* Who changed the email and phone number again on 3 April?
* Have we taken the necessary steps to kick the scammer out of the account?
* What data does the hacker have access to via the fleet portal, particularly re drivers?

* There’s already a dedicated section in the Global category in the KB for Beehive features and how-to guides called *Beehive guides*, which contains many Beehive-feature-related articles -  including articles covering features such as [summary of the case, rephrasing|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/71576?country=global&language=en], [smart replies|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/9986331533074?country=global&language=en], etc.
* Creating a new summary article in the same section likely wouldn’t improve either visibility or awareness. If agents aren’t finding the current articles, they may not find this one either. From a content perspective, it’s quite counterintuitive to create a separate article pointing to resources that already live in the same place.

*Outdated content & maintenance*:

* Many of our existing Beehive guides need a thorough review and update, as some have become outdated, as was already highlighted in the [Slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C032D4ZGZR6/p1743789000099409?thread_ts=1743772231.894069&cid=C032D4ZGZR6] you linked.
* We currently don’t have a plan and/or capacity to tackle this in Q2, and there’s no confirmed timeline for when we can include reviewing and updating Beehive guides in our roadmap.
* Creating a new “summary” article would mean linking to content that may already be inaccurate, and each time something changes, we’d have to remember to update both the original guide and the summary article, increasing our team’s administrative overhead.

*Technical limitations (images)*:

* At the moment, our tooling prevents us from uploading images to the KB, which is especially helpful for how-to guides like these. This limitation makes it challenging to create or maintain comprehensive articles with visuals. While how-to guides can be created without visual aids, some articles would be much better if visuals could be included. 



Given these challenges, a single overview article might not actually solve the visibility and awareness issue and could introduce ongoing maintenance concerns. We fully appreciate the intent behind the suggestion and are aligned on the importance of improving how agents learn about Beehive features—but for now, no changes to the KB will be made.  

That said, we’ll explore the possibility of including reviewing the Beehive guides KB section in our Q3/Q4 plans to ensure it’s accurate, complete, and helpful. 

Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions or concerns. I’ll go ahead and close this ticket for now.

Thank you, and have a nice day! 🙏

*4.29 Arbetsrättsliga villkor för taxiförare*
4.29.1 Leverantörens åtagande
Leverantören ska under hela ramavtalets löptid tillämpa kontraktsvillkoren enligt punkt 4.29.1–
4.29.4. Ramavtalet ska fullgöras i enlighet med de vid var tid gällande arbetsrättsliga villkoren
avseende lön, semester och arbetstid enligt bilaga 1.
De arbetsrättsliga villkoren i bilaga 1 benämns ”Villkoren”.
Leverantören ska säkerställa att Villkoren uppfylls av anlitade underleverantörer som direkt
till att fullgöra ramavtalet, oavsett antal mellanled. Leverantören ska också säkerställa att dessa
underleverantörer medverkar vid uppföljning enligt punkt 4.29.4.
Åtagandet gäller för anställda arbetstagare när dessa utför arbeten enligt ramavtalet. Vilka
arbetstagare eller vilket arbete som omfattas av de arbetsrättsliga villkoren framgår av bilaga 1.
Åtagandet avser arbete som utförs enligt svensk arbetsrätt
4.29.2 Justering av Villkoren under kontraktstiden
Under kontraktsperioden kan kollektivavtalet som Villkoren utgår från omförhandlas av parterna. Om
kollektivavtalet omförhandlas äger Sjöfartsverket rätt att justera Villkoren. Justeringen kan avse lön,
semester och arbetstid, exempelvis vilka lönenivåer som ska tillämpas.
Om Villkoren justeras kommer Sjöfartsverket skriftligen underrätta Leverantören om detta.
Leverantören ska därefter, senast inom 30 dagar från det att den mottog en sådan underrättelse,
börja tillämpa dessa justerade Villkor.
4.29.3 Hur villkoren kan uppfyllas
Leverantören kan uppfylla Villkoren för lön, semester och arbetstid genom att tillämpa dessa.
Leverantören kan även uppfylla dem på följande alternativa sätt:
genom att vara bunden av och tillämpa ett centralt kollektivavtal som tillämpas i hela Sverige på
motsvarande arbetstagare i den aktuella branschen eller ett lokalt avtal som bygger på detta
avtal,
• genom att tillämpa villkor för lön, semester och arbetstid i ett centralt kollektivavtal som
tillämpas i hela Sverige på motsvarande arbetstagare i den aktuella branschen utan att vara
bunden av det, eller
• genom att vara en arbetsgivare som omfattas av en utstationeringssituation enligt lagen
(1999:678) om utstationering av arbetstagare och tillämpar villkor om lön, semester och
arbetstid i enlighet med denna lag.
• Ovanstående gäller även för eventuella underleverantörer.
*4.29.4 Egen rapportering*
På begäran av Sjöfartsverket ska Leverantören senast två (2) veckor från det att begäran mottogs
skriftligen redovisa hur Villkoren efterlevs.
Redovisningen lämnas i formulär enligt bilaga 2: formulär för egenrapportering. Leverantören ska
lämna den rapportering som framgår av bilagan och på begäran kunna styrka lämnade uppgifter.

*4.30 Kvalitetssäkring*
För att säkerställa efterfrågad kvalitet i uppdraget ska Leverantören ha dokumenterade rutiner för
kvalitetsledning i sin verksamhet.
Kvalitetsledningen ska minst omfatta en implementerad kvalitetspolicy.
Det åligger Leverantören att ha ett strukturerat och dokumenterat kvalitetsarbete vilket ska:

* vara aktivt under hela avtalsperioden och leda till ständig förbättring,
* följas upp internt minst en gång per år och
* organiseras av Leverantören som själv ser till att samtliga krav som relaterar till kvalité i avtalet
efterlevs.
På begäran av Köparen ska Leverantören lämna giltigt certifikat enligt ISO 9001 eller beskrivning av
kvalitetsarbetet enligt ovanstående punkter.
*4.31 Miljöledning*
Sjöfartsverkets leverantörer ska arbeta aktivt för att begränsa miljöbelastningen av sin verksamhet.
Miljöledningen ska minst omfatta en implementerad miljöpolicy.
Det åligger Leverantören att ha ett strukturerat och dokumenterat miljöledningsarbete vilket ska:
* vara aktivt under hela avtalsperioden och leda till ständig förbättring,
* följas upp internt minst en gång per år och
* organiseras av anbudsgivaren som själv ser till att samtliga krav som relaterar till miljö i avtalet
efterlevs.
På begäran av Köparen ska Leverantören lämna giltigt certifikat enligt SS-EN ISO 14001 eller
beskrivning av miljöledningsarbetet enligt ovanstående punkter.

*4.32 Uppsägning av avtal*
Köparen har rätt att med en uppsägningstid om tre (3) månader säga upp Avtalet, eller avbeställa
lagd order om uppsägningen/avbeställningen kan motiveras av;
• myndighetsbeslut som Köparen inte kunnat råda över, eller
att förutsättningarna för fullföljandet av leveransen, utanför Köparens rådighet, har ändrats i
väsentlig omfattning och det med hänsyn till detta inte är rimligt att fullfölja leveransen.
•

Leverantören har rätt till ersättning för utfört arbete och nedlagd styrkt självkostnad. Vid uppsägning
ska resultatet av helt eller delvis utfört arbete redovisas och överlämnas till Köparen. Efter
överlämnandet får resultatet av leveransen användas på samma sätt som om leveransen fullföljts.
Utöver vad som anges ovan har Köparen rätt att säga upp Avtalet med omedelbar verkan i enlighet
med 17 kap. 17 § punkterna 1 och 3 LOU eller när Avtalets takvolym har uppnåtts.

* *4.33 Hävning*
Vardera Part har rätt att med omedelbar verkan häva del av Avtal eller hela Avtalet om den andra
Parten inte fullgör väsentlig förpliktelse eller på annat sätt väsentligen bryter mot detta Avtal och
rättelse inte sker inom 30 dagar efter skriftlig erinran därom.
Köparen äger därutöver rätt att med omedelbar verkan häva del av Avtal eller hela Avtalet om det
framkommer att
Leverantören lämnat oriktiga uppgifter i sitt anbud eller på annat sätt i samband med
upphandlingen och dessa uppgifter varit av väsentlig betydelse vid bedömningen av tilldelning av Avtalet,
Leverantören försätts i konkurs, inleder ackordsförhandlingar, inställer sina betalningar, ansöker
om företagsrekonstruktion eller annars kan anses vara på obestånd,
•
• maximalt vite till följd av tre enskilda beställningar har utgått,
• Leverantören inte uppfyller de obligatoriska kraven i upphandlingsdokumenten,
• Leverantören eller dess företrädare är föremål för utredning om korruptionsbrott,
Leverantören vid tidpunkten för beslutet att tilldela Avtalet eller under avtalstiden befinner sig i
någon av de situationer som avses i 13 kap. 1-3§§.
•
Leverantören under tiden för fullgörandet av Avtalet träffas av förbudet om fullgörande av
kontrakt i Rådets förordning (EU) nr 833/2014 om restriktiva åtgärder mot bakgrund av
Rysslands åtgärder som destabiliserar situationen i Ukraina.
•

Part som är orsak till hävning ska ersätta motpartens direkta skäliga kostnader som uppkommer till
följd av hävningen (t ex men inte uteslutande kostnader för ny upphandling och merkostnader under
den avtalslösa perioden).

* *4.36 Skadestånd.* 
** Leverantören ska ersätta och hålla Köparen skadeslös för alla skador, förluster, anspråk, kostnader eller utgifter som Köparen åsamkas till följd av Leverantörens avtalsbrott. Leverantörens ersättningsansvar omfattar inte indirekt skada eller följdskada. 
** *Leverantörens maximala ersättningsskyldighet ska inte överstiga 120 prisbasbelopp.* 
*** 2025 är prisbasbeloppet *58 800 kronor*. 
*** *58 800 kronor* x 120 = 7 056 000 kr 
** Vid skada som vållats uppsåtligen eller
genom grov vårdslöshet ska ansvarsbegränsningen inte gälla.

*Arbetsrättsliga villkor:* 

* Som tidigare anfört och som visat sig tydligt efter medial bevakning, vi måste se över hur detta ska hanteras i våra avtal med underleverantörer/FO bör vara medvetna om detta krav om de inte redan är det.

Hi,

Sharing an update on FinReg opinion on the intended partnership with Amilon. 

After additional discussions with the Amilon team, it is clear that under the setup Bolt would be in the role of gift card issuer and remain the liable party for the financial services licensing risk. The Amilon setup is not aligned with our financial services licensing risk approach and therefore from FinReg risk perspective we would not advise issuing gift cards under this setup. 

The setup offered by Amilon, where Amilon distributes Bolt gift cards in exchange for funds payment by either a B2B customer of Amilon or the end-user, means that Bolt will be issuing prepaid gift cards. This is not our standard approach (vs for example our Bolt Business coupons use case which is fully a post-paid scheme).

Highlighting again the risk that in the EU we are relying on the commercial agent licensing exemption to be able to mediate our basic marketplace payments. We need to be acting only on behalf of the sellers of service on our platform. This means that in order to manage the risk that we may fall outside of the licensing exemption, we should not take on any roles where we can be seen to act also *on the side of the buyer/payer in the funds flow.* This includes avoiding setups where we will be issuing prepaid instruments to app users.

Regarding *risk impact*, this activity is medium to high risk from FinReg perspective, as it may impact also our ability to mediate marketplace payments in general in the country. The regulator would require us to ensure compliance with the commercial agent licensing exemption by terminating the gift card activity and also the remaining balances, but meanwhile they may also require us to *disable all in-app and Bolt Business payments* in the country until compliant. Prepaid instruments issuing will also increase the likelihood that the regulator becomes interested in reviewing Bolt’s overall reliance on the commercial agent licensing exemption for payment mediation. So this is the risk that we would be taking. Practical risk mitigations could be considered, e.g. only very limited use cases when instruments are issued with little visibility on the market, and limited volumes, but I guess this would not be aligned with business expectations for the partnership, since scaling the gift cards scheme will still remain an issue.

*For parallel, please consider that for the same risk reasons we also have not enabled our user top-up functionality of Bolt Balance.* So the question remains, why take a different approach than with our own top up functionality for users.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*QUESTIONS FROM TFL*
{panel}

*Log-in attempts*

* When a check is triggered, circa every 30 days, a driver cannot access the app until a check is successful and Bolt is confident that the person completing the verification check is the driver permitted to fulfil bookings. Can you confirm:
** (i) How many attempts the driver is permitted to complete the verification process.
** (ii) The time limit for completing the verification process.
** (iii) If drivers have a further opportunity to pass the check before their account is suspended.
** (iv) The reason(s) a driver may or may not be granted an opportunity to submit another selfie image following a failed check.
* Please describe all security features designed to prevent access to the account holder’s app by someone other than the account holder.
* Please provide flowcharts and other relevant diagrams that comprehensively illustrate and detail both the front and back end of Bolt’s app during failed and successful log-in attempts.

*Calculation*

* Please confirm if artificial intelligence is involved in a geo-location verification check, and if so, the extent of its use and its purpose. We would like to better understand the extent and degree of human involvement in the Onfido driver identity verification process. Please provide an explanation outlining Bolt’s human intervention and quality assurance processes
* You have explained in previous correspondence and in meetings that a driver fails the check because where/when they begin the verification process and where/when they complete the process is sufficiently far apart and in as short a period of time as to be physically impossible. Please confirm what this threshold is, how it was determined, and how Bolt calculates it.

*Communication*

* We would also like to know how a failed check is communicated to the driver. Furthermore, is the driver made aware the check failed due to a discrepancy in the geolocation of the two devices involved in the log-in attempt, and, if so, how? We would appreciate copies of the messages sent to a driver in these circumstances.
** We are concerned, in the circumstance that the driver’s selfie passes the biometric verification check, but the driver fails the verification check due to a geo-location discrepancy, that without clear communication that the biometric check passed and the driver identity check failed for another reason, the technology appears to the driver to have erred in its judgment.

*Appeals and investigations*

* We would like a full description of the process and procedure Bolt follows during the 30-day appeal window, from the driver being restricted from accessing the app to their reactivation or dismissal. Please provide flowcharts and other relevant diagrams that comprehensively illustrate and detail the procedures followed during the appeal window. Please include the tasks performed by each agent when reviewing the check failure and the factors considered when making their decision. It is particularly important to understand the opportunities the driver has to satisfactorily explain the reason for the failed check.
** As explained in our Quarterly Meeting, TfL has received feedback from the Court that it is necessary to demonstrate that we have made our licensing decision based on all relevant facts and not solely on Bolt’s interpretation of them and its ultimate decision to dismiss a driver. Whilst Bolt may not need all the information available to it to arrive at a decision, we may find it useful in our own investigation and ask that you outline all possible evidence you rely on such that we may request it, as appropriate, following a notification of a driver dismissal.

*Data*

* Please confirm all other data that may be considered in Bolt’s review of a failed verification check, for instance, booking data or the driver’s home address. We would appreciate if all data considered by Bolt agents in their review is made available to us when we conduct our own review of the driver’s fitness to hold a Private Hire Driver Licence. It is important for us to understand the logic behind Bolt’s decision making and be presented with equivalent information to arrive at our own conclusion. Please identify any information available to Bolt in its decision-making process that it is unable to share and the reasons it is unable to do so.
* It is our understanding that the location of the devices used to log-in to the Bolt app is determined using the same Global Positioning System (GPS) signal used by Bolt operationally, for instance, when providing customers with the Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) of or displaying the PHV as it arrives at a pick-up point. Can you confirm the raw data is the same and explain the importance of the accuracy of this data to Bolt in its operations.
* We would like to understand how and when Bolt collects location data. For example, we would like to know if data is only collected when a driver has logged into the app and has it open, if it is collected when the app is running in the background or if Bolt tracks data even if the app is not in use.
* Please explain how Bolt identifies the different identities of the driver’s devices and how and when this information is collected. We understand that some devices use their own biometric verification for users to access the device. Is this something Bolt considers as part of its investigation into a failed check?

First, for all markets we will try to assess how different the [variance|https://bolt-datascience.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/309348310889482?o=3829506390716583#command/309348310889483] between android and ios will be (with the same approach as in simulations in MMM Validation V2):

* We run a regular OLS regression of android on ios (or vice versa)
* We assess the MAPE of the fit.
* It is expected that we see better fit for metric without tourists than the metric with tourists.
** NOTE: MAPE is the metric here that also takes to account the scale of the metric (just comparing std of residuals might not be correct, because there are naturally less locals than all users)
* Here’s some initial summary of results. [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pTx7Pgz5PnY5TCrY0b0rpMVcHlL9a6ueWfmL0GM60Lg/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pTx7Pgz5PnY5TCrY0b0rpMVcHlL9a6ueWfmL0GM60Lg/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link].  It seems that there’re markets which definitely take advantage of locals (Abuja, Lagos, Baku, Valletta, Lisbon), for many it does not seem to be real advantage. And for some - it seems to actually even increase the variance.

A couple of notes:

* I’d generally still revise the approach one more time, since for some markets having locals seems to increase android-ios variance (which is a bit counterintuitive)
* Variance takes to account fluctuations that we are adding ourselves with ads (which might be skewing the measurements)
* Such results might be of different application to experiments. Remember that experiments are taking more short-terms results as learning and testing period (and inflow if tourists might be skewing a 1Y long model not so much, but be crucial for )

Main conclusion I’d draw from the models is:

* We previously used to think that tourists make time series generally better ordered and reducing noise overall
* But they seem to just add big biases on the market, overall level of noise seems to stay even if we’re looking at locals only.

To clarify:

# *Verification Requirement*
The verification needed involves the user sending a clear photo of themselves holding their ID, ensuring that the name on the ID matches the name on the account. This step is required when a user requests to change their phone number. The same process also applies when they request to change their payout number.
# *Reason for the Change*
We’re making this change following a recent incident where a rider from ride-hailing reported that a number we updated for a courier actually belonged to him, and he had no affiliation with the courier in question. This new verification process will help us prevent such cases of mistaken identity and ensure we can confidently confirm ownership of accounts before making any sensitive changes.

I hope this answers your question

* The indemnity in DTI’s [+T&Cs+|https://drivertechnologies.com/privacy-policy/#terms-and-conditions] is between DTI and its users. It offers no protection for Bolt, and so DTI’s recent references to the T&Cs is not relevant.
* The draft [Promotion Agreement|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cgj61WqspBConIVgA9kVG0yNhxdS_81LlSLo3wKAq6E/edit?tab=t.0] between Bolt and DTI contains a high-level mutual indemnity at clause 8. It also contains a limitation on liability provision, but it seems the limit (USD 500) does not apply to indemnification obligations. As such, clause 8 is the focus.
*  I would suggest replacing Clause 8 with the following:
** “_Counterparty will defend, indemnify and hold Company harmless from and against all third-party claims, damages, liabilities, losses, expenses and costs (including reasonable fees and expenses of attorneys and other professionals) to the extent arising out of or resulting from Counterparty’s breach of this Agreement, Counterparty Branding, or Counterparty’s products and/or services. Counterparty will also, at all times during and after the term of this Agreement, hold harmless and indemnify (at its own expense) Company on demand against any claims, loss, damages, costs or expenses and other liabilities (including but not limited to legal fees) incurred by Company arising out of or in connection with:_
*** _any failure by Counterparty, its employees, subcontractors, or agents to comply with applicable data protection laws;_
*** _any personal data breach (concerning the personal data of a user of Company’s services) suffered by Counterparty or caused by Counterparty (whether directly or indirectly);_ 
*** _any data subject rights requests received by Company from users of Company’s services which concern recordings made through Counterparty’s video recording technology platform; and/or_
*** _any complaints or disputes concerning recordings made through Counterparty’s video recording technology platform that contain or relate to users of Company’s services._”

# main IPO related mandate: 
## Termination (Section 16 of the 8 Nov 2024 amendment to EL). We can terminate the engagement at any time by way of giving 28 days' prior written notice to PJT. 
## Fees are as follows: (i) retainer (Q.- 200kEUR) fees accrued up to termination date are still due (i.e. for the 28 day notice period as well); and (ii) in case there is an IPO (or other Transaction - incl primary raise) within 12 months from termination the success fee element (3MEUR) is also due.
## resuming in the future - since we don’t have a specific timeline in mind I think it makes sense to terminate (following the procedure described above) and then entering into a new agreement with PJT should we want to resume the process.
# secondary add-on:
## Termination: same as above (same termination clause applies to the two mandates as per 8 Nov amendment). I.e. termination is done by way of 28 days' prior notice and can be done with respect to either an Equity Capital Markets Transaction or a Secondary Transaction (or both). 
## Fees: success fee due in case there is a company-organised 50M or higher secondary transaction in the next 12 months involving investors included in the process conducted by PJT (but excluding our existing investors, e.g. Sequoia).

My overview of how renting a car via Turo’s website looks like in the UK and France in terms of standardised conditions:

* Insurance information disclosed in the vehicle card, after the vehicle is selected.
* Turo offers 3rd party liability insurance apparently hired by Turo itself. The information about protection is very limited in the UK and a slightly more detailed in France, with maximum coverage amounts.
* Turo is license as a resident insurance producer for property and casualty and surplus lines in the following jurisdictions as per its insurance license disclosures: [https://turo.com/us/en/policies/additional-policies#insurance-license-disclosures|https://turo.com/us/en/policies/additional-policies#insurance-license-disclosures|smart-link] .
* However, Turo also has this disclaimer in their Terms: *_Insurance and protection plans._* _Turo is not an insurance company and does not insure hosts or guests. Host and guest protection plans made available through the Services are in no way related. To be eligible for the benefits of a protection plan, hosts and guests must comply with these Terms. Protection plans are available through the Services only in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada (excluding any of the territories and the provinces of Manitoba and Saskatchewan), France, and Australia. Please refer to the_ [_specific terms for guests_|https://turo.com/gb/en/policies/terms#specific-terms-for-guests] _and_ [_specific terms for hosts_|https://turo.com/gb/en/policies/terms#specific-terms-for-hosts] _sections below for additional information based on the nature of your use of the Services._
* No information about insurance coverage for the vehicle itself in the vehicle card.
* Important provisions regarding insurance found in [Turo’s terms of service|https://turo.com/gb/en/policies/terms], in sections named “Specific terms for guests” and “Specific terms for hosts”, indicate that insurance coverage is not standardised.
* Turo seems to offer protection plans for hosts with respect to physical damages to their vehicles. The conditions vary from country to country.
** [https://help.turo.com/en_us/detailed-explanation-of-protection-plans-or-uk-hosts-B16_INxV5|https://help.turo.com/en_us/detailed-explanation-of-protection-plans-or-uk-hosts-B16_INxV5|smart-link]

Hi [~accountid:712020:a5a185f8-f29b-419b-aaf4-7d504ef74d14] coming back to checkout recommendations compliance with DSA. 

*SUMMARY: Are we legally required to*

* *turn the "info" symbol into a "sponsored" tag?* - yes, but we have some wiggling room here 👇 
* *tag individual products with "sponsored" tag? -* yes, but we have some wiggling room here 👇 





+*A. PRODUCT RECOMMENDATION AS AN AD:*+

If products are displayed on a checkout recommendations bc some partner or brand has paid, etc for it then this product recommendation is seen as an ad *=> DSA applies.* 

+*B. GENERAL MARKING VS ITEM SPECIFIC MARKING:*+

According to the DSA we as a platform need to ensure that {color:#ff5630}*each specific advertisement presented*{color} on our platform is clearly identifiable as an advertisement. This means that each separate item under the recommendations which is displayed there as part of promotion is seen as specific advertisement. Hence, if we want to be *100% compliant* then we should probably mark each item which is sponsored as an ad *=> tag individual products with “Sponsored” tag.*

*However, considering that:*

# Bolt Market also uses generic tag “I” next to the Categories section, i.e. not marking individual category tabs/products with tags
# the exact interpretation of an ad and how it should be marked is still to be discovered (see my note [below|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-49136?focusedCommentId=3180843])
# from UX perspective it might look very “noisy” for the user’s eyes

*then for now, if adding separate tags to sponsored products require too much development from your side, then I think the risk is low-mid if we use generic marking next to the “Recommendations”.* 

❗ However, it should be very clear for the customer if the click on the tag what exact products under the recommendations are sponsored - i.e. who has paid for it, how advertises it , why they see this ad. 

+*C. TAG TITLE - “SPONSORED” vs “I”*+

To be 100% compliant then we should use a tag named “Sponsored” or “Ad” instead of an “I” button. Mainly, since we use the same “I” button also for all the other information which might not be related to advertisements and hence, it might not be enough clear for the customer that they might find ad related info under that button/tag. *From legal perspective using “Sponsored” or “Ad” would be preferred.* 

If we want to use “Sponsored” or “Ad” tag for the recommendations section, then we should probably use the same type of marking for all the other sponsored/ad related content on our platform (i.e. under Bolt Market, with search results, etc) so that the approach would be unified. This would be recommended from legal pov, however I understand that this again may require additional engineering, etc and hence not be possible for now. 

*Hence, it is ok to use “I” button to tag sponsored content under the recommendations in a checkout if:*

# same approach is used with other sponsored content on Bolt’s platform
# we don’t have resources to develop/apply “Sponsored” / “Ad” tag instead for all the platform
# until any of the authorities have made specific request to change it

After checking over Uber and Wolt then I see that they use more distinctive marking for sponsored content by using “Sponsored”  marking. Considering this + compliance part then we should plan for moving over to “Sponsored” or “Ad” tags in general in the future.

The main arguments that *Bolt* is presenting in its defense against *Mikel Vila Burdell's* claim are as follows:

+Principal argument:+

# *Admissibility of the Claim*:
#* *Bolt* argues that the claim is inadmissible because the legal entity being sued, *Boltest TXFY, Sociedad Limitada*, is not the correct party. *Boltest TXFY* is a subsidiary that does not have any contractual relationship with passengers or service providers (i.e., independent drivers and fleet partners) and only provides administrative support to other entities within the Bolt group. The actual contractual relationship between the passenger (Mr. Vila) and the platform is with *Bolt Operations OÜ*, an entity registered in Estonia.

+Subsidiary arguments:+

# *Responsibility for the Incident*:
#* *Bolt* emphasizes that it is not responsible for the incident where Mr. Vila missed his bus. *Bolt* claims that the company acts solely as an intermediary between passengers and transport service providers and cannot be held accountable for issues related to the quality or delivery of transport services.
# *No Liability for the Missed Bus*:
#* *Bolt* highlights that Mr. Vila requested the ride on the day of the incident (February 2, 2025) at 13:25, which was close to the departure time for his bus at 14:00. In summary, *Bolt's defense* centers around the argument that *Boltest TXFY* is not the responsible entity in the contract, that *Bolt* is merely an intermediary and not liable for transport-related issues, and that the incident was caused by Mr. Vila's timing and not by any fault of the company.

h3. *. Contacting Drivers – Earnings Communications*

h4. *What’s driving this initiative?*

This is part of a broader push to improve transparency and engagement with drivers participating in the Bolt Car program. To put it bluntly, the *lack of awareness* from the drivers perspective drives their sense of a *lack of transparency* which in turn affect their *engagement and performance* in the Vehicle financing program. We’ve noticed interest from drivers around earnings clarity and wanted to proactively communicate this data in a secure and structured way, while reinforcing the value proposition of the program. The idea here would be to make it clear to them what they are receiving (because they are already receiving it as is) but more importantly +*why*+ are they receiving it . We would stay factual and not give more information than we already do, which is essence would be restricted to # of rides and earnings of # rides (which is very easy to ccalculate as it’s only 2 euros x # rides) Clear process of this is already in place, with the historicals to show for. Happy to share it with you if needed 

h4. *Content of the communications*

The draft template has still not been defined, but would likely include:

* A single, final earnings figure for the period (no detailed breakdowns or tax codes)
* A reminder of the Bolt Car program benefits
* A privacy disclaimer and opt-out mechanism, as per your recommendation

We’re happy to run the final version by Legal/Privacy once ready.

h4. *Input from GFT/Legal*

No formal review from GFT or reclassification teams has been done yet — this note from you is our starting point to align with the right internal stakeholders before proceeding. I have had conversation with Philippine to go over whether this would constitute a reclassification risk, which she confirmed. The idea of the ticket was to get all my answers in one go in order to see how to proceed forward with the project

h4. *Entity responsible*

The emails would be sent by *Bolt Services France SARL*. Please confirm if you would recommend otherwise.

Not urgent but in my plans for Q2 rollout, in order to tweak it in Q3 (when activity is not at peak) to go full steam ahead for Q4. For me this would all happen ideally in app. WIth vehicle financing not being uniform across all regions (due to the nature of regulations across countries) we all have a distinctive ways of operating. Which is why this hasn’t been rolled out as a whole for the stream. Would be happy to roll it out via the app but this would take a lot more time and effort across multiple departments and not sure if it brings added value to my counter parts in other countries (certain of them operate on a fleet basis, others not, reclassification is an issue for some but not all) 

----

h3. *2. Leaderboard-Style Gamification System*

h4. *What’s driving this?*

We’re exploring ways to incentivize driver performance in a fun, non-monetary way, with full anonymity. The goal is to foster friendly competition, boost engagement, and help new drivers feel more part of the community.

This idea is currently in early-stage brainstorming, not yet included in the MVRA. We agree that global alignment is important, and this wouldn’t be rolled out locally without coordination and proper risk assessment.

h4. *Metrics used for ranking*

Still to be finalized — but early suggestions include:

* Number of rides completed (for now, maybe in the long term other metrics would be considered driver rating for example, but not in FY2025) 

All data would be aggregated, anonymized, and not tied to bonus payments (at least in the current version). We are open to modifying this based on legal/privacy input. The only way i would see us remunerating them for this would be potentially a quarterly bonus tied to it not even sure if it should be monetary ( tickets, Bolt merh, vehicle accessories) 

h4. *Next Steps*

Thanks for the reminder — we’ll complete the Preliminary Privacy Risk Assessment and share it with your team so you can conduct a more formal review.

----

Let me know if you need any more information in the meantime, or if it makes sense to set up a quick sync

*Q1: What does Certn consider a second chance?*
Certn does not prescribe a specific “second chance” policy. While this is not legal advice, we generally recommend that employers implement a thoughtful, consistent process when a background check returns as “not clear.” Rather than automatically disqualifying a candidate, many of our clients include a step for human review and provide the candidate with an opportunity to respond or clarify the findings.For example, we generally advise against automatically rejecting applicants based on an initial “not clear” result. Instead, applicants should be given the opportunity to dispute the findings, something we understand your current policy already [http://supports.In|http://supports.In|smart-link]  cases where the “not clear” result remains unchanged after a dispute, and the applicant cannot provide any insight, some clients choose to offer the applicant the option to obtain a certified, fingerprint-based criminal record check from a local police service. As a consumer reporting agency, Certn does not have access to the specific information determining a “not clear” status only the police can review that level of detail. Again, this is not a mandatory step, but one that some employers adopt to support fair hiring practices and reduce the risk of discrimination claims.



*Q2: How is this different from disputes that drivers submit to Certn for issues with background checks?*
It’s not. Reviewing and resolving disputes is a fundamental part of the background screening process, and we expect this to be reflected in your hiring policy. As noted above, we are not recommending anything additional beyond the usual dispute process.When an applicant disputes a criminal record result, Certn works with our police partner to review the information. If the results are updated, the revised report is issued to you and should be the basis for any hiring decision, not the original report.If the results are not changed following the dispute, what you choose to do next is entirely up to you and should be governed by your own internal policies and legal guidance.*Client* 



*Q3: How do your clients typically manage Second Chance opportunities (i.e., in Certn, outside Certn, etc.)?*
When an enhanced criminal check returns as “not clear,” most clients notify the candidate and offer them the opportunity to dispute the results through Certn. We then work with our police partner to reassess the record. If the results are updated, the revised report should be used as the basis for any hiring decision.If the results remain “not clear” after the dispute process, next steps vary depending on the client’s internal policy: some may choose not to move forward, particularly where their policy allows for disqualification based on unresolved findings, others may allow the candidate to obtain and submit a certified fingerprint-based criminal record check from a local police service before making a final decision.Additionally, with respect to basic criminal record check results, depending on the role and the nature of the conviction (if applicable), some clients may proceed with hiring regardless of a conviction if the offense is not directly relevant to the job duties. In certain provinces, non-discrimination laws may require this type of individualized assessment. However, this is very much industry and jurisdiction-specific, and we are not in a position to advise on your specific [obligations.It|http://obligations.It]’s important to remember that enhanced criminal checks can include any interaction with law enforcement, not just charges or convictions. That’s why it’s critical to have a thoughtful, well-documented hiring policy informed by your legal counsel, your industry standards, and the type of work your employees perform.

Hello Team!

I completely understand why this might look like a double charge, but I can assure you that the user was only charged once. This is a common part of how card payments are processed. Here's what happens:

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


The refund is successfully completed. I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba

* On 12 March 2025 (5am UTC) , a malicious third party (the "*Scammer*") gained access to the [+account+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet-company/companies/edit/105550?tab=profile] (the '*Account*") of a fleet owner (the "*FO*").

** {color:#ff5630}Unclear how the scammer gained access to the account{color}.
* While in the Account, the Scammer took the following actions:
** Changed the email address and phone number.
** On 24 March 2025, they messaged CS asking to change the bank details on the Account.
*** Scammer submitted a selfie / photo of ID taken from another conversation between CS and the FO. This was not caught.
*** Scammer submitted out-of-date company documents. This was not caught.
*** Bank details were successfully changed on 27 March, and the Scammer was able to redirect a payout of EUR 2769.37.
* With access to the Account, the Scammer would have had access to the following data:
** FO:
*** Profile Data (including name, email, phone number, profile picture, fleet company name, preferences and settings);
*** Payment Data (including IBAN and tax number of the fleet company);
*** Identification / Verification Data (although ordinarily copies of ID documents are not visible on the fleet portal, they are visible in communications with Bolt CS - this is how the Scammer was able to source a copy of the FO's selfie and ID); and
*** User Generated Data (including contents of communications with Bolt CS).
** Drivers (6 active):
*** Profile Data (including name, contact details, profile picture, date on which they started as a Bolt driver, preferred destinations and fleet company details);
*** Vehicle Data (including model, year, number plate and number of seats);
*** Identification Data (although copies of ID are not visible on the fleet portal, the expiry date of driving licences is);
*** Geolocation Data (the Scammer would theoretically be able to see the live location of active drivers who are online via the fleet portal);
*** Payment Data (including last four digits of payment method, bank account number and sort code, invoices, compensations, balance reports, tax reports and payouts); and
*** Trip Data (including order history).
* On 3 April, the FO noticed that they had not received their payout (which, in turn, is hindering the FO's ability to pay their drivers). The FO wrote to Bolt CS to complain.

** On 3 April (12:30), the FO changed the password on their account.
** On 4 April, payouts were disabled on the Account, such that the Scammer could not redirect any further payments. Password was also changed.
** Email and phone number have been changed back. Bank details have also been reverted.
** No signs of malicious activity since then.
* As at 10 April, the FO has continued to write to us over the past few days expressing their concern and threatening escalation.
** We are processing the refund to the FO.

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

hey [~accountid:63f5cbd9c1f7acaf636c1cae] , the profilings went live this week. I’ve pulled some data specifically for Zakopane, and I have a suggestion. 

to start off, the problem size seems to be very small as of now (at least according to data from the last 3 months). with the profilings data, we have aggregate data to make smarter decisions to block users or not. 

let me share some parameters I’ll use:

* long cancel: it’s a cancellation that happens when at least half of the order’s predicted ETA has already passed. for example, if the pickup ETA is 6 min and the cancellation happens after 3min, we’ll consider as a long cancel, if not, then we don’t. these long cancels are the ones that are more meaningful for fake orders as the bad actors' intent is to waste time from our drivers. 
* ratio of long cancels: count of long cancels divided by the total number of cancellations
* avg wasted time from drivers: on average how much time drivers are spending in minutes from the cancelled orders

my suggestion is to create a rule that will block users for a whole week if they reach at least 4 long cancels in the last 3 months with a ratio of long cancels of at least 50% and avg wasted time from drivers >= 2 min. OR if they have 3 long cancels, with ratio >= 0.75. with these conditions, we would’ve blocked 39 users that had cancellations in Zakopane in the last 3 months. they had a total of 894 cancellations, where 778 were long cancels. we spent 240 euros compensating cancellation fees related to these cancellations and had a 1.1k euros cost in CS tickets. and the sum of GMV from these users was only 320 euros. 

after getting their account unblocked, if they have another cancel, they’ll be scheduled blocked for another week. if they continue active and cancelling, once the costs reach the global thresholds, they get hard blocked. 

how does that sound to you? do you have any objections or are you ok with this suggestion?

* There will be a *pop-up titled “Join Bolt Rewards and benefit from Partners offers” (or equivalent - tbc)*, which includes *marketing and data sharing consent*.
* We’ll follow a *risk-based approach*:
** The consent will be *voluntary*, not mandatory. If we made it mandatory, we couldn’t claim it’s valid consent.
** The consent pop-up will have two clear options: “I agree” / “I disagree/not interested” – this is the more legally defensible approach.
** The risk is lower conversion, which we’ll monitor. But we will also *contract drivers who did not give consent*, and if challenged, our position will be that *the consent option was provided*, and contacting those who didn’t consent was an operational oversight. 
* Consent will be effective *immediately*, and T&Cs won’t need to be updated.
* If a driver has contacted CS and asked to be removed from the contract list, we should not contact them again.

It is relatively simple to calculate gnss orbit parameters at any time point and location, using
[https://github.com/shashwatak/satellite-js|https://github.com/shashwatak/satellite-js|smart-link]  where the source data is coming from [https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=gnss&FORMAT=json|https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=gnss&FORMAT=json] (needs to be refreshed ca 2 times per day, or less, if minor precision loss is accetable)

this
[http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/tools/sats.php|http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/tools/sats.php]

calculates gnss satellite elevations and altitudes for given coordinates for current time (columns elevation/azimuth), cur current time + 1 hour (columns elevation +1h/azimuth +1h).

ublox columns indicate which satellites are included in ublox-filtered dataset from ublox gnssNowOnline (looks like it filters by elevation >0 in given time precision period).

green indicate satellite presence in curresponding dataset. in my calculation include satellite if elevation > 10deg (looks better to exclude those way too low)

There is good match between own-calculated parameters and ublox-calculated parameters. 

It seems some newer beidou and galileo satellites are not included neither in ublox or quectel files.

Additional filtering can be performed by device capabilities (L5 satellites included or not)

gnss-filtered celestrak file has 146 satellites
unfiltered ublox file - 108 satellites
unfiltered quectel file includes 120 satellites

As said already, some newer sats are missing from ublox/quectel files. 

statistics:
for whole Europe at one point in time the file would need to include ca 75 of 146 (ca 50%) satellites
for one city at one point in time, the file would include 40..47 of 146 (27%..32%) satellites. tested with Europe only, coverage elsewhere might be slightly different

for a file for whole Europe we would need to include ~50% of whole satellites tes, ie simple filtering by shard would give us ca 50% file size win over current unfiltered file, both for ublox and quectel

the optimal solution would be to use file-per-city approach, which would give ~70..80% win over current unfiltered file.
this could be relatively implemented so that backend would implement http endpoint where the query includes iot id, and then backend could look up in which city the device should be and return corresponding file, and the iot would query over http, instead of mqtt.

Hi [~accountid:5b306883ed67e12dd27645e1] - I have created Jira tickets to summarise the Privacy advice on Project Green features (Phase 1). This ticket is intended to deal with drivers having multiple profiles / being able to switch between models seamlessly.

As previously discussed, there are {color:#36b37e}*no significant blockers*{color} on this from a Privacy POV. However, {color:#4c9aff}*I do have the following questions before I can provide my final advice*{color} on our compliance position. Please feel free to add anyone to this ticket who would be able to assist with answering these questions:

# I understand that to separate out the models, drivers will have one profile ID for driving under the agency model and one profile ID for driving under the principal model. Based on this:
## How will it be clear on Admin whether a driver is acting under the agency or principal model? *Where will this be shown in the backend*?
## Will drivers also have *separate profile IDs* for (a) driving as a _fleet_ driver under the agency model; and (b) driving as a _fleet_ driver under the principal model? I assume so, but just to confirm.
## Is the current intention for drivers to *sign up* *_separately_* *under the agency and principal models* (such that they need to verify themselves / provide compliance documents each time)? Or if the driver registers under one model, will they be ‘fast-tracked’ if they then want to sign up for the other? This is definitely a question be discussed with Legal, but I wanted to check from your side as well. 
### *If drivers sign up separately, will we be transferring any data we already have on them into their new profile*? (e.g., let’s say a driver sets up a principal model profile and uploads a profile picture. One month later, they set up an agency model profile - would they be asked to upload a fresh profile picture, or would we simply use the one we already have?).
## Presumably, other than giving drivers separate profile ID for agency and principal activities, there will not be any other segregation of their information on Admin? *How will this look to Bolt employees looking through their profiles on Admin*?
## Will drivers have *separate acceptance rates  / average ratings* under their agency and principal model profiles? I assume not, but just to check.
# I understand that the intention is to share _all_ driver / passenger data between Bolt Services UK Limited (for the principal model), Bolt Operations UK Limited (for the agency model) and Bolt Operations OU (for the wider business). *I assume there will be no optionality for users in terms of the data that is shared* for now (i.e., will users have any control over / be able to object to any data sharing in this context, depending on the category of data)?
# *Will we be keeping a detailed log* of exactly when a driver is driving under the agency / principal model, and when they switch between profiles? If so, please let me know how this will be designed, as we will need to find a way to be able to export this / provide it to drivers if asked.
# *Will there be any segregation in the back-end* (i.e., on Admin) of a driver’s data under the agency and principal models in relation to the following categories of data: (i) order history; (ii) online time; (iii) scheduled rides statistics; (iv) login sessions; and (v) vehicle history? How will these look on each of the driver’s profiles in Admin?

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Subject to the above, my general advice would be the following from a Privacy POV*:

* Unless there is a good reason not to, try to *ensure clear segregation of users' data (agency vs. principal model) on Admin*. This is primarily because if we receive a data subject request from a user asking for specific data under one of the models, we need to have means of extracting this efficiently.
* *If drivers sign up separately and we intend to re-use any of the data we already have on them / transfer it to their new profile, let me know*, as I will need to think about whether synchronising certain data categories is proportionate / within users' expectations.
* We should *keep a log* of exactly when a driver is driving under each model.
* Any profile suspensions (including where a driver is suspended under one model as a result of being suspended under the other) should continue to have *manual review* rather than being full automated.
{panel}
