Hi Team - I have created Jira tickets to summarise the Privacy advice on Project Green features (Phase 1). This ticket is intended to deal with mid-order substitution (i.e., Driver A substituting an order to Driver B).

As previously discussed, there are {color:#36b37e}*no significant blockers*{color} on this from a Privacy POV. However, {color:#4c9aff}*I do have the following questions before I can provide my final advice*{color} on our compliance position. Please feel free to add anyone to this ticket who would be able to assist with answering these questions.

[~accountid:5b306883ed67e12dd27645e1] 

# What data about a potential Driver B would a Driver A need to fill in on Driver A’s Portal to invite that Driver B to be a substitute?
# I understand that if a driver has a ‘Driver A’ profile and a ‘Driver B’ profile, these will be segregated by different profile IDs. On this point:
## Will a driver have separate Driver B profile IDs for every Driver A on whose behalf they are acting as a substitute? Or will they only have one profile ID for all cases in which they are acting as a substitute (regardless of the Driver A).
## We previously discussed that Driver A profiles would effectively become ‘shadow fleets’ where they have Driver Bs acting as substitutes. Can you provide a but more context behind what this means in practice? How will this appear in Admin?
## Where on a driver’s profile will it be listed that the driver is a main driver (Driver A) or a substitute driver (Driver B)?
# If a driver suspended / banned from the platform, presumably they would not be able to use substitution (i.e., registering as a substitute driver) as a means of getting around this?
# When will we be able to see the designs of how substitution will be presented to riders?
# I understand that Driver A can remove Driver B from their list of substitutes at any time. On the other hand - would Driver B be able to remove themselves from Driver A’s list? If so, how?
# If Driver B rejects the order, have we decided on how the order will then be re-allocated?
# What information about Driver B will be visible in Driver A’s app / profile once Driver B has agreed to act as their substitute?
# How will ETA factor into the determination of which Driver Bs are available for a order reallocated from Driver A?

[~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8] [~accountid:6083d099c998c200691f2ab3] 

# Do we now have visibility on the full list of documents we will be asking Driver B for as part of the process for registering them as a substitute driver? Does this currently differ in any way from the list of documents we are ordinarily requesting from UK drivers when registering them on the platform? I am particularly interested in any criminal records / background checks.

[~accountid:712020:209f6e12-e421-4fbf-9a9f-60d100117bab] 

# Apologies if we are re-treading old ground here, but just so I have this centralised - What will the contractual relation ship be between Driver A and Driver B? Will they need to agree to a specific set of T&Cs?
# I have seen contradictory statements regarding whether Driver A does or does not reviewing Driver B’s compliance documents as part of onboarding. I assume our position remains the former?

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Subject to the above, my general advice would be the following from a Privacy POV*:

+Invitation emails sent to Driver B:+

* Where Driver B is _already a Bolt driver_, we should *ensure a link to the* [+*driver privacy notice*+|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides] *is included in the email invitation*.
* Where Driver B is not yet a Bolt driver, we should *include the following disclaimer language in the email*. This is because the driver privacy notice will not yet apply to Driver B, but we are still processing their personal data - since we do not yet have a ‘third party privacy notice’, we need to fulfil transparency requirements through another method. We are finalising our analysis on the red text and I will provide an update on this:
** _“Bolt has collected your contact information from another driver for the purpose of (per that driver’s request) inviting you to act as their substitute. Bolt processes your contact information based on its legitimate interest in allowing drivers to create a list of substitutes (thereby ensuring that the services provided by drivers are flexible). If you do not accept this invitation, Bolt will delete your contact information after_ {color:#ff5630}_[a reasonable period / 30 days]_{color}_. For further information on how Bolt processes personal data, please refer to Bolt’s privacy notices.”_

+Rejection by Driver B+

* If Driver B does not accept the invitation from Driver A, we should *delete Driver B’s contact information* (which was provided by Driver A) *within a reasonable period* (e.g., 30 days).
* We should also *introduce a functionality that allows Driver B to remove themselves from Driver A’s list* of substitutes at any time. If Driver B made this request to Bolt, it would count as an objection request (which we have to action by law unless we have a good reason not to).

+Display in app+

* Once Driver B accepts an invitation and appears in Driver A’s list of substitutes, *we should minimise the amount of information about Driver B that is visible in Driver A’s platform / app* (e.g., just include their name and profile picture). This is because, if Driver A’s account is hacked, we want to make sure scammers do not have access to much information about other drivers (to minimise the impact of the hack).

+Contractual relationship+

* This is more of an FYI - Depending on their contractual relationship, Driver A may need to enter into a data processing agreement with Driver B. However, this is ultimately Driver A’s responsibility (not Bolt’s), and we want to avoid exercising control over the terms that Driver A enters into with Driver B - as such, I will work with Product Legal to include provisions in the Driver T&Cs that cover this (i.e., by requiring Driver A to respect data protection obligations - cc. [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] just for visibility based on what we discussed on our last call).
{panel}

Business Benefits

This provides you with the flexibility to:

* Hide fields you don't use. 
* Require fields that are important to you.

Changes

* Academic - Annual Work Period
* Academic - Work Period Percent of Year

* Employee Type

* Frequency
* Job Profile
* Which team will this person be moving to?
* Who will be this person's manager after the move?
* Work Hours Profile
* Location

h3. What Do I Need to Do?

From the *Configure Optional Fields* task, select the Change Job functional area.

Configure the fields for your company. 

Test your configuration and update your training materials.

Proposed technical solution to stop people form requesting more than 28 days within a year.

* Created a new validation (based on Option 1 - requirements) that looks at the total number of already approved remote work days and deducts the number from the maximum allowed (28) if the requested # days is more than 28 - already approved days it will trow an error. However, as people can request remote work upfront (e.g. 2026) this raised the issue of “granting” another 28 days for next year. In order to accommodate this we will built an evaluate expression field that will evaluate which is the year the requester is adding remote work for then evaluate the number of remaining days.

h2. Description

Evaluate the possibility of updating the current Hire Process to ensure hires do not appear on Slack before their contract is signed.

*Description:*
The current process results in new hires becoming visible on Slack via Okta integration even before their employment contract is signed. This creates potential issues, such as:

* Visibility of individuals who may not officially join.
* Miscommunication among teams regarding the hire's status.

*Proposed Change:*

* Adjust the process so that the Okta integration and subsequent Slack visibility are triggered *only after the contract has been signed*.
* Ensure this change aligns with compliance and minimizes disruptions to the onboarding workflow.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# A hire does not appear on Slack until their contract is signed and confirmed in Workday.
# Okta integration triggers only after the contract is marked as signed in Workday
# Communication and documentation on the updated process are shared with relevant stakeholders.

Workday can only create or disable accounts in Okta. When a user is manually deactivated (edit workday account -> account disabled); Okta workflows picks that every hour and deactivates it.The problem arises from a different flow from IT side. They also have a second flow, where every 14 days, a deactivated account is also disabled/deleted. When Workday sends new joiners data, if the account is deactivated, they do not create another one. However if it is deleted, Workday will tell Okta to consider that worker as a new joiner.The problem for us is that a manually deactivated account will get deleted in 14 days, and Workday then will say, oh, not deactivated, create a new user

Solution: Sergiu will not delete after 14 days the accounts we manually disabled; so when Workday comes with data it sees account was disabled.However, Sergiu wants to delete those accounts, so when termination was processed in Workday we need to inform him to delete those accounts, and we will work on a Make automation to do that

We are *removing the "credit" limit clause from the special terms templates.*
As an [example|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wT9xRPC07hAYnFUd7RJV-dwXf2wb5qk5vdEParroo9U/edit?tab=t.0] see c. 2.1.

*Why?*
It's a legacy practice to reflect it in the agreement and it has never been needed for legal purposes as such.
For some time now we have had this information available in the Company Dashboard per Business account. Meanwhile it consumes resources to keep the limit up to date in the agreement documents.

*When?*
As of now.
We'll remove the relevant clause from the templates in [Confluence|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3482320952/Templates.+Business+account] and Spotdraft asap but expect to finalize by end of March.

*What do be mindful of with new customers?*
Make sure the accurate limit is reflected for each account in the Company Dashboard.
By default we shouldn't mutually be agreeing on the limit but rather we assign each company a spending limit per their profile.

*What do be mindful of with existing customers?*

* Any changes to an existing limit should be well communicated to the customer (ideally in advance and ideally via Dashboard - if available). Especially when increasing the limit based on Bolt's initiative.
* No need to amend the currently signed special terms just for this reason but do remove this clause when an opportunity arises (i.e. smth else triggers the need for amendment in the agreement). However please be mindful that until the clause remains in the agreement it should be kept strictly aligned with the limit shown to the customer in the Dashboard.

*What if a customer itself wants to see this reflected in the agreement?*
Please check out the FAQ in [Business Legal Confluence|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923692552/FAQ.+Business+account.+Legal] (under Fees, Payments & Refunds). Any questions - please share in the thread

Update following a discussion with Marcel and Mariann on the pre-analysis and upcoming steps. Here's a summary:

*Recap:*

* The experiment will run in Nigeria, Poland, and Thailand, with a 50/50 split between treatment and control groups.
* Conversion rate is defined as the number of users who take a ride during the experiment period. Since the treatment group won’t receive email comms, alternate engagement metrics aren’t reliable.
* Null Hypothesis: Stopping marketing emails to inactive users has no impact on the likelihood of taking a ride (i.e., conversion rates and GMV remain unchanged between test and control groups).

*Pre-analysis:*

* Sample size: Each market has a large enough pool of inactive users to detect a 5% minimum detectable effect (MDE) with sufficient power.
* Experiment duration: In March 2025, we reached over 90% of inactives in each country within the first 14 days of the month. Given our large user base, a *14-day* experiment window should be sufficient to detect meaningful effects.
* Detailed calculations and reasoning are available in this [doc|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TQ1qYC1CTrzrPB3CsyGA5HwPjZBtzxUCiEhOIquUct8/edit?gid=1795233558#gid=1795233558].

Hi Team - I have created Jira tickets to summarise the Privacy advice on Project Green features (Phase 1). This ticket is intended to deal with price bidding.

As previously discussed, there are {color:#36b37e}*no significant blockers*{color} on this from a Privacy POV. However, {color:#4c9aff}*I do have the following questions before I can provide my final advice*{color} on our compliance position. Please feel free to add anyone to this ticket who would be able to assist with answering these questions.

[~accountid:5b306883ed67e12dd27645e1]

# I understand that we will be retaining details of specific price bids for each trip. How will this be visible in Admin? If this is only available in JSON, is there a way to make it available on a more obvious Admin page?
# I understand that we will not be using previous bids made by a driver or a rider to influence the  price setting algorithm for future trips - is that still correct? If so:
## Will we be using the price bids submitted by users for any other purposes beyond price setting (e.g., general analytics  assessing user trends over time)? If so, please list them (this may be a question for Ops [~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8])
## Will price bids have any impact on work allocation / how eligible riders are found for a trip offer? I assume not, but I just wanted to check.

[~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8] [~accountid:6083d099c998c200691f2ab3] 

# Do we intend to publish any guidance materials / blog posts / help centre articles on how price bidding works?

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Subject to the above, my general advice would be the following from a Privacy POV*:

+Data storage+

* I understand that drivers and riders will only be able to see their final price for trips in the app / portal, rather than bidding history. This is not an issue, but we can expect users to request this information via data subject access requests. We therefore need to *ensure that: (i) bidding history for each trip is clearly visible on Admin; and (ii) this information can easily be extracted from Admin in bulk* (in case a user asks for their _entire_ bidding history).

+Transparency+

* Given the interest of the UK regulator in price setting and transparency, it would be preferable to *publish at least one comprehensive guidance article on how price bidding works* (in particular, the data used / how this influences price / how this does not influence work allocation or future trips).

+Profiling+

* It is important that we *ensure that a user’s bidding history does not in any way affect: (i) how they are allocated future trips; (ii) how future trips are priced*. Nor should price bids in any way affect the baseline calculation of an estimated price. Given the UK regulator’s interest in the algorithms / data behind price setting, we need to avoid situations where we are profiling users in this context.
{panel}

I have received the following input from the law firms, inserted in its full: 

*  *Finland:* 
** {color:#006644}*Unfortunately there are no public databases available where we could perform a search by using the provided keywords*{color}. 
** What we could in practice do is to (a) do a Google search in the Finnish media (by way of example, according to the media the number of reports of sexual offences conducted by taxi drivers during 2023 and 2024 was more than 50) and/or (b) reach out to District Courts registries and ask for information about violent and sexual offences in relation to taxis. 
** The District Courts will charge a fee for providing the information, which fee we would know only once the amount of documentation would be known.   
* *Sweden:* 
** *Källor och täckning:* Varken databasen Juno eller Sveriges Domstolars söktjänst innehåller samtliga rättsfall som kan vara relevanta för er. {color:#006644}*För att uppnå en något mer fullständig täckning skulle det krävas att båda dessa källor används parallellt*{color}. Fr en fullständig sökning hos respektive domstol i Sverige skulle dessa behöva kontaktas direkt eftersom inte alla avgöranden publiceras digitalt. Tidsåtgången (och därmed även kostnadsbilden) påverkas av om det ska vara en sökning genom (i) båda databaserna samt (ii) kontakt med varje domstol, eller (iii) avgränsat till en viss källa. Det kan inte garanteras att resultatet av en sökning genom endast en databas är fullständig eller statistiskt heltäckande.
** *Omfattning av sökningar:* Flera av de sökordskombinationer som listats genererar ett stort antal träffar – i många fall flera hundra per sökning. Samtliga träffar är dock inte nödvändigtvis relevanta för den information ni efterfrågar (domar kopplat till vålds- och sexualbrott i taxibranschen). Exempelvis inkluderar en sökning på ”misshandel + taxi” även domar där en person åkt taxi före eller efter en misshandel, utan koppling till själva taxiverksamheten som sådan. {color:#006644}*För att säkerställa att sökträffarna faktiskt är av relevans för den sammanställning ni efterfrågar krävs en individuell genomgång av varje träff*{color}. Detta kan vi göra antingen genom att läsa igenom samtliga domar eller genom att göra en första gallring endast baserat på rubrik och sammanfattning. Det går att göra en relativt enkel grundläggande sållning av vad som är relevant, men givet den stora omfattningen av träffar är det tidskrävande och innebär samtidigt viss osäkerhet kring träffsäkerheten och tillförlitligheten av resultatet.
** *Nästa steg:* Tidsåtgången och därmed även kostnadsbilden påverkas av hur omfattande arbetet ska vara, framför allt beroende på om ni önskar inkludera en eller flera källor för sökningen (se punkt (i)-(iii) ovan), och nivå av granskning för att bedöma relevans (t.ex. individuell sållning av respektive dom). Vi återkommer gärna med ett konkret estimat så snart vi vet mer om hur ni önskar att uppdraget eventuellt ska avgränsas och genomföras.

So overall based on the incident we observed multiple issues which could indicate on the underlying issue in AWS: 

# The first one what was originally raised by Mehran.  So we have nodejs service running in AWS EKS clusters live-euc-1-alpha and live-euc-1-bravo which had timeout when was trying to connect to redises in another AWS EKS cluster which located in other account 598800702182.   We use AWS VPC CNI so all the pods are have uniq IP for communicate with these redises. And nodejs service which was running in eu-central-1b zone got timeout error when was trying to connect to redises.  
#   This one what Artur mentioned, is timeout in communication between microservices.  So we have nodejs service running in AWS EKS clusters live-euc-1-alpha and live-euc-1-bravo. When service A send request to Service B it's looks in this way:  Service A -> sent request to internal k8s svc to reach envoy-internal pods -> envoy internal pods send request to IP of pod (from AWS VPC CNI).   So based on collected data, when service A trying to reach internal svc in eu-central-1b zone, we also got timeout.  
#   Another case:  We have EC2 in main account (737418964414) which distribute across 3 az (eu-central-1a/eu-central-1b/eu-central-1c), which sent request to [node.live.boltint.net|http://node.live.boltint.net] address, which with AZ specific DNS resolve, sent requests to specific AZ to NLB which has in target pods from live-euc-1-alpha and live-euc-1-bravo cluster. And EC2 in eu-central-1b also faced with timeout when tried to sent requests. The strangest thing that from NLB perspective healthcheck of target all were healthy.  


Based on these cases AWS performed the investigation and found that they had underlying issues with network equipment. Answer from AWS:



After thorough investigation, we have identified reported timeouts and connectivity problems in the eu-central-1b availability zone. During our analysis, we identified a hardware incident in the AWS infrastructure (eu-central-1b) that occurred during a similar timeframe (approximately 13:50-15:52 UTC on March 31st). The impact was limited to instances located in this specific availability zone during the period of approximately 13:50-15:52 UTC on March 31st. Upon further review, our team examined EKS logs and found no other significant issues. While we observed higher-than-normal outbound bandwidth usage on certain network interfaces, which may have contributed to the disruption.  

 Currently, the underlying hardware issue has been resolved, and we are continuously improving measures to prevent similar hardware-related incidents in the future. Our infrastructure teams have already addressed the affected hardware components.



So nothing to do here anymore, issue confirmed outside or responsibility area.

# The official TiDB prelive must not contain synchronised Live environment data.
# If synchronization from Live to Prelive is absolutely necessary, the target schema must be limited in size to avoid impacting the stability of the prelive cluster.
# Due to technical limitations, synchronization to TiDB Prelive must be paused during the migration phase until the Live environment has also been fully migrated to TiDB.

We strongly recommend disabling selective synchronization to the MySQL prelive environment prior to initiating the TiDB migration.

* Aside from privacy considerations, please check with [+local GFT+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3600842870/Global+Field+Team] (if you have not already done so) whether we have grounds in our T&Cs for preventing drivers from re-registering in this way.
+Retention of data after account deletion+
* We already retain certain data about a driver after their account has been deleted. We are allowed to do so under data privacy laws, provided that we are only retain what is strictly necessary and that we have a good reason for doing so.
* It would be helpful to understand exactly *what additional data we want to retain here* - is it phone number? Email? This is a factual / operational question than a privacy question, so please let me know.
* If, for example, we need to retain a driver’s phone number to prevent them from re-registering, then we must ensure that we do so in a proportionate manner. What this means in practice is:
** (1) Only taking this step where we are confident that the driver has definitely acted fraudulently. We should ensure we have evidence to back this up.
** (2) Only retaining information that is strictly necessary to ensure the driver cannot re-register.
** (3) Ensuring that the decision to prevent the driver from re-registering was not fully automated, and was instead reviewed / made by a human.
** (4) Ensuring that our usual appeals / review processes are available to the driver when we prevent them from re-registering.
+Transparency / comms+
* Please check with local GFT, but we should make sure we are somehow notifying drivers that we will prevent them from re-registering due to breaching our platform terms. This will prevent driver submitting complaints / questions regarding why they cannot re-register.
* When drivers initially request the deletion of their account, CS should have guidance on the comms to send to drivers confirming that we are working on their request. This should contain language which effectively says “_We are deleting your account. Please note, however, that certain information may be retained after account deletion in accordance with our privacy notice_” (check the GS guidance for the actual wording). We must ensure such language is always included in the comms - this will mitigate the risk of drivers accusing Bolt of retaining their data without their knowledge.

* EU consumer law requires that key commercial practices are clearly communicated before purchase. Please see below for my assessment of the agreement:

*LEGAL AND CONTRACTUAL RISKS*

h4. 1. *Ambiguity of Terms and Objectives*

* The agreement is *vague* and lacks precise legal definitions (e.g., "strategic actions," "activation campaigns," or "visibility").
* There is *no stated duration*, nor provisions for renewal, early termination, or specific termination causes.

_Recommendation:_ Include a clause specifying the term of the agreement, termination rights, and define key terms clearly.

----

h4. 2. *Overly Broad Commitments Without Clear Counterparty Deliverables*

* Bolt commits to designing campaigns, participating in events, and supporting sectoral communication without a *clear obligation from España de Noche* to deliver tangible results.

_Recommendation:_ Clearly state that any participation or support will be subject to Bolt’s prior approval and that no automatic obligation is assumed.

----

h4. 3. *Communication Plan – Reputational Risk*

* The agreement foresees *wide public communication* of the collaboration without requiring Bolt’s *prior review or approval*.
* Bolt’s brand would be visible in various external channels, potentially leading to *reputational exposure*.

_Recommendation:_ Add a clause requiring prior written consent from Bolt for any use of its name, logo, or branding in public or media communications.

----

h4. 4. *Studies and Awareness Campaigns – IP and Cost Risks*

* The plan includes conducting studies and launching campaigns, but responsibilities, budget allocation, *ownership of resulting materials*, and *use rights* are not specified.
* Bolt might fund campaigns without having clear control over their content or how the results will be used.

_Recommendation:_ Define responsibilities, intellectual property rights, and usage rights. Make all activities subject to prior budget approval and scope definition.

----

h3. *FINANCIAL CONSIDERATIONS*

* España de Noche will receive an *annual payment of €20,000 + VAT*.
** However, there is *no detailed scope of deliverables* or deadlines linked to this payment.
** It is explicitly stated that *production costs for campaigns are not included*, potentially exposing Bolt to undefined expenses.

_Recommendation:_ Request a detailed breakdown of what the fee covers and clarify that any additional expenses (e.g., campaign production) must be pre-approved in writing by Bolt.

----

h3. *MISSING OR RECOMMENDED CLAUSES*

* No *confidentiality*, *applicable law*, or *dispute resolution* clauses.
* No clause addressing the *non-exclusivity* of the collaboration or denying any agency/representation authority.
* No reference to *personal data protection (GDPR)*, which may become relevant in joint campaigns or communications.

_Recommendation:_ Include standard clauses covering:

* Confidentiality
* GDPR compliance
* Dispute resolution (preferably mediation or arbitration)
* Governing law (e.g., Spanish law)
* No partnership or agency relationship
* Non-exclusivity

----

h3. *Summary of Key Recommendations*

# Define duration and termination terms.
# Clarify scope of collaboration and ensure all obligations are mutual and measurable.
# Maintain control over communications and brand use.
# Protect against unapproved costs and undefined deliverables.
# Include standard legal protections (confidentiality, data protection, governing law, etc.).



----

My reasoning for this is as follows:

* The requestor is from the Home Office - as such, they are from a (relatively) trustworthy governmental organisation that specialises in immigration law issues, rather than from an unknown third party that would raise eyebrows.
* The data being requested is very limited and not particularly intrusive. Verifying the document simply helps to prove it is not fake, whereas the date on which the user created a Bolt account is not particularly intrusive.
* I appreciate that the requestor has provided a couple of different legal bases (which is odd in the circumstances). However, I think it is difficult for us to argue that we absolutely *_cannot_* disclose this data given that:
** The requestor comes from ‘an official authority' and the request is proportionate (which may pass the Article 6(1)(e) UK GDPR test at a push);
** Even though the requestor has not specified what “crime(s)” they are investigating in the context of relying on Schedule 2, Section 2 of the DPA 2018, applications for permission to stay in the UK involve criminal background checks (which, in turn, would involve verifying those checks by reaching out to organisations like Bolt). As such, it is not unreasonable for the Home Office to be requesting this kind of information.
** Part I Section 20 of the IAA 1999 concerns requests relating to immigration control (applications for permission to stay logically fall under ‘immigration control’), and the data being requested seems proportionate.
* *In short* - although the Home Office has been a bit shaky in citing a solid legal basis, I think would could defensibly argue that it was legitimate for us to share this information if we were ever challenged on this. We can therefore share the information IMO - however, since Gab previously though the legal basis was insufficient, maybe sjut sense-check this with her first.

+For a high level summary here:+ 
Spin, one of the operators of e-scooters and e-bikes in DC is suing DDOT after being denied operating permits for 2025-2026. Spin alleges the denial was arbitrary, unfair and unconstitutional. They are seeking injunctive and declaratory relief to remain operational in the District. The Preliminary Injunction hearing is set for 11 April. There is specific mention of Hopp having preferential treatment because we got some deadline extensions and grace periods others did not receive. 

GFT legal counsel concern was: if the preliminary injunction is granted, could the court (later down the line) rule that the permit to Hopp was improperly awarded? In any event, should Hopp take some proactive/defensive action at this point in respect of the PI hearing e.g. intervene etc? 

The advice from Baker&Hostetler was as follows: 

_Darin and my litigation colleagues advise that_ *_Hopp intervention would not be beneficial at this point and in this posture of the case_*_.  The relief requested by Spin in the complaint focuses on bringing Spin back into the scooter contract, as opposed to challenging the grant of licenses to other vendors._

_Unlike the Columbus, Ohio proceedings involving the exclusive award to Veo, the contract award here is not exclusive.  In other words, a preliminary decision in a lawsuit brought by a disappointed bidder for a nonexclusive contract would not jeopardize the contracts that DC entered into with other parties._  

_Although it is conceivable that a broad order by the court to re-evaluate the bids could certainly work to the detriment of Bolt/Hopp,_ *_there is not much that Bolt/Hopp could offer to the court to influence its decision.  It is up to the DC government to defend its procurement decision, and my colleagues noted that the DC government may not appreciate the intervention by Bolt/Hopp at this point_*_._

Recording here the external advice that we received in connection with the possible driver earning ads: 

_As disclaimers cannot be relied to correct the general impression created by the main copy, there is risk under Canadian law with proceeding with this copy given the nature of the qualifications on which the claim is made. My concern with the current version of the main copy is insufficiently clear about the likelihood of a driver reaching the amount given the qualifications._

_Ideally, the claim should be revised to reflect that it is an average for top drivers. So something like this:_

               _Top drivers can earn as much as $X per week driving*_

_I would recommend not using the daily claim (up to $X daily) unless the calculation is based on actual daily earnings figures (as opposed to an extrapolation from weekly or monthly earnings)._

_With respect to the disclaimer, can you please clarify what the “net” calculation is (i.e., “net average earnings”). I assume it refers to earnings after the portion of the ride fare payable to Hopp has been deducted, but please let me know if my understanding is incorrect._

_Based on that assumption, I recommend revising the disclaimer as follows:_

_*Based on the net average earnings of the top 15% of driver partners in GTA and assuming a 7 day week of driving 7.5 hours per day. Actual earnings may vary considerably, as it depends on the number of rides, ride distance, time and location, weather, demand, driving area and other external factors. You may make more or less than this average amount. Earnings include fares, certain campaigns (which may change and vary by location). No minimum earnings are guaranteed and are not paid by Hopp._

_Note that I have also assumed that the calculation is in fact based on GTA drivers._

_Note that the disclaimer should appear on the same page as the main copy. There will be higher risk if there is a requirement to link through to the disclaimer given the importance of its clarification of the general impression._

Call yesterday with DE competition law outside counsel. The proposed blacklist exchange between Bolt and Miles is not forbidden by DE antitrust laws to the extent there’s a legitimate interest (safety) for both the operators and the society. 

However, exchange and consequences should stay focused on safety and extreme cases, and the exchange of information must be limited to the necessary in order to achieve this goal.

Once the initiative becomes known, there’s the risk of other competitors reaching out to Bolt and Miles and requesting access to the same information. There wouldn’t be reasonable grounds to deny access, since it’s based on legitimate interest and safety. However, Bolt would then be in a position to negotiate and get access to the other competitors' blacklists as well.

Also briefly discussed and confirmed the integration of competitors to Bolt’s platform per se shouldn’t be forbidden by competition laws. Recommendation was to monitor Bolt’s and similar aggregation examples within the industry in case authorities start auditing them.

I’m going to put these into the announcement, but not sure how helpful it is.

+*CONSENTS / PERMISSIONS*+

* Marketing at Bolt (genral)
** Unless it is for partner consents, we rely on soft opt-in (i.e., soft-opt in for all _Bolt_ marketing materials).
** In terms of explicit wording of partner marketing consent, I requested this from Driver LCM team (Hunzala Khan) [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/D08PX0Z7P0W/p1745924558909049], and there is no specific consent wording - the user just ticks boxes for ‘Partner Offers’ per medium of communication (e.g., email, text etc.).
* Soft opt-in:
** This can only apply in the following circumstances:
*** Contact details obtained during sale (this applies).
*** Marketing is for similar products or services (this applies - it is for two branches of Bolt ride-hailing. It is not a separate product line like financial services).
*** User must have a clear means of opting out at all times (we can ensure this).
*** Bolt must instead rely on legitimate interest (we can do so).
** As such, {color:#36b37e}*we can rely on soft opt-in*{color}. A compliance gap is with regards to conducting a LIA (we need to do one for marketing generally) but this is in the backlog.
* Permissions across profiles:
** Current position:
*** Asked [+here+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08GT6EUS23/p1744715477363759]. Response was: “_Currently_ *_consents are stored on a "partner" level,_* _which means that same values remain in sync between multiple driver accounts that belong to the same person ("partner"). With Project Green we allow to have multiple Driver accounts under the same Partner, but many things, such as Marketing Consents, are shared between these accounts. It will be quite difficult to change, and especially in v1._”
*** [+Link+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08GT6EUS23/p1745930501611239?thread_ts=1744715477.363759&cid=C08GT6EUS23]: “_Hey! From the Lifecycle side, 1 single consent across models is preferred. This extra complication can lead to even more errors down the line, and since the user can switch models whenever and however often he wants, this can also affect what types of communications he receives. Example: We send a communication for model A, the user has consent for it, but the comm has a delay of 30 minutes, and the user will receive it even if he switched models, and for model B, he does not have that particular consent. Let’s keep the same consent at partner level as we had before_”.
*** Basically, all profiles have a single Braze account. If driver opts into partner offers on one profile, they automatically opt in on the second profile.
** Since different entities will be sending the marketing comms, need to consider whether synchronisation of consent is a sustainable approach.
*** Under ICO guidance, consent must be specific to the form of communication.
*** I have asked Kost for his views [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/D07AFGZ3V6F/p1745498577322969]. Response was: “_My idea is to ensure that any comms that are unique to the specific "profile" can be managed in this separate profile; for the rest of the comms, those are synchronised across profiles_” - This seems sensible to me. I flagged this to stakeholders and asked if this is something they can implement (Mihai Tanase, Hunzala Khan, Alexander Fokau) [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08GT6EUS23/p1745924332862299?thread_ts=1744715477.363759&cid=C08GT6EUS23], they said no.
** Advice:
*** Preference would be to have profile-specific consents kept to profiles, but it sounds like this will not be feasible.
*** As such ([Link|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08GT6EUS23/p1746180525965299?thread_ts=1744715477.363759&cid=C08GT6EUS23]):
**** Lets ensure drivers have clear understanding that the marketing preferences are the same in both profiles:
****# For this, I can suggest a disclaimer in the Communication Preferences: _"These Communication Preference applies to both your _ and _ profiles."_ No strict rules on where the disclaimer is placed as long as its clearly visible to drivers.
**** Lets ensure that the driver preferences are correctly reflected in both profiles - i.e. if a toggle is off in one profile, its always off in the second profile.

This seems to be caused by a known design decision of the booking system where booking capture is done in 2 steps

# cover the entire shadow-credit from user’s balance making the balance negative (user is now in debt)
# money received from the external provider will then move to cover the balance

If the user is unlucky and creates another booking between those 2 steps then the 2nd booking will include the temporary debt from the first booking

Capturing of the 2nd booking will follow again these 2 steps and the result will be user having positive balance for the additional money we got from the customer

Goes pretty harshly against commerce moto “we do not mess with customer’s money“. But this supposedly happens very rarely and there is no clear easy fix for this.

Payment analysts have been asked to come up with numbers how often does this actually happen compared to how often people actually complain to CS. Depending on the outcome we will need make a decision if this is worth investing into

Dear Md Hasan,

*Notification of a personal data breach*

We are writing to inform you about a recent incident.

*What happened?*

On 25 March 2025, we were made aware of instances of phishing activity. Individuals falsely holding themselves out to be members of the Bolt Support Team may have asked for information from you to gain access to your Bolt account. This may have resulted in temporary, unauthorised access to your account. However, we are not aware of anything that indicates that your information is at any further risk.

As this type of activity relies on tricking customers into providing account details, it can unfortunately still occur despite appropriate security measures. As such, we have outlined below some steps you can take to protect your account from this type of activity.

*What steps have we taken?*

Bolt is committed to addressing these incidents and has robust measures to prevent, limit, and mitigate unauthorised access to customer accounts. These measures include (but are not limited to) requiring authentication via a one-time password to access customer accounts from new devices when attempting to log into an account using a phone number. In addition, we mask rider and driver phone numbers on the Bolt app to preserve privacy and improve security.

As soon as we became aware of this incident, we immediately took action to ensure your account's security further and mitigate the potential for any adverse effects. These actions include (but are not limited to) rolling out guidance materials on Bolt’s in-app Stories platform to educate customers on avoiding phishing attacks. We are continuing to take steps to enhance our security and to protect the information within our care.

*What is the potential impact?*

Our investigations indicate that some of your information may have been accessed as a result of phishing. The information that may have been impacted was limited to the information that would have been accessible on your Bolt account during the limited period of compromise, which may have included any of the following:

* Profile data (including name, contact details, home address, display image, date on which you started as a Bolt driver, and company details);
* Vehicle data (including model, year, number plate and number of seats);
* Identification data (including UK driving licence number and expiry date);
* Payment data (including last four digits of payment method, VAT number, bank account number and sort code, invoices, compensations, balance reports, tax reports and payouts);
* Communication data (including the contents of any open conversations with Bolt Customer Support from the previous 120 days); and
* Platform usage data (including order history).

We are unaware of anything to indicate that any of your information has been stolen, and our investigations indicate that the incidents were opportunistic attempts to divert trip payments from driver accounts or make unauthorised trips from rider accounts.

*What should you do?*

As precautionary measures, we recommend that you remain vigilant regarding your personal information, including any financial accounts. Consider refreshing and avoid re-using online passwords. Be alert to any unusual requests for access to your data or credentials via email, in-app messages, telephone calls or any other means of communication - in particular, we suggest never sharing your phone number, email address and one-time verification codes with strangers.

If you have any questions about this message, please let us know by responding to this message. Please be sure to include (i) your questions and (ii) an explicit reference to this message / the personal data breach so that your questions can be allocated to the correct team.

We take your privacy and the security of your information very seriously and apologise for any inconvenience that this may cause.

Yours sincerely,

*Head of Privacy & Data Protection Officer*

Due to the actual size of the tire the lowest seat position is higher than initially specified. 

Initially: 743mm

Actual: 750/760mm

+30mm due to the cabling conflict results with: 780/790

Conclusion: For safety purposes the users may express need to be able to put their leg to the ground while sitting on the seat waiting for the green light on a traffic light for example. Perhaps they prefer this kind of seat height more than comfort riding positioin. Is it preferred to put full sole to the ground or just standing on tiptoe is not clear since any user test or interviews have not been carried out specifically about this topic. The only test related to the seat height was Mad-Max general ergonomics test. One of the participants at least expressed their need to adjust the seat according to the possibility to reach to the ground. 750/760mm seat height meets barely the requirement. Standing on the tiptoe in this case might be possible. 

From riding position point of view higher than 750/760mm seat height, let's say 780/790 mm still enables 1.5m person to adjust the seat for comfort riding position.
